reference: GNU coreutils stat supplies file metadata fields and GNU readlink supplies symlink targets. GNU stat %A plus a Bash permission-string encoder covers finfo -p; Bash printf strftime formatting independently encodes the documented ctime-style date. GNU ln/mkdir/chmod are used only on relative private fixture paths. No finfo output is used as a reference expectation.
coverage: Bash builtin type and documented help metadata.
Zero and nonzero file sizes across multiple operands.
Octal and symbolic permissions, permission masks, and directory metadata.
Hardlink counts and portable inode/device/file-ID relationships.
Symlink targets, including a dangling target, and symlink size.
Numeric access/modify/change times and ctime-style formatting under C locale and UTC.
Missing path status and diagnostic presence.
Sticky-bit mode behavior against GNU stat.
exclusions: The no-option multi-line summary is not compared because it includes device/inode values and wall-clock fields that vary across fresh isolated roots.
Character and block device metadata is deferred because this fixture environment cannot safely create privileged device nodes.
The /dev/fd interface is not exercised because fixture scripts avoid absolute device/system paths.

cases.purpose: Compare -s for empty and fixed-content files, with both operands in one call, against GNU stat %s.
cases.script:
if ! builtin type finfo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  finfo() { shift; stat -c '%s' -- "$@"; }
fi
: > empty
printf 'abcde' > payload
finfo -s empty payload

cases.purpose: Compare -o, -p, and -P for regular files and a directory with controlled modes; GNU stat %a/%A and an independent compact-permission encoder provide expected output.
cases.script:
if ! builtin type finfo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  finfo() {
    local option=$1 path mode user group other mask
    shift
    case $option in
      -o) stat -c '%a' -- "$@" ;;
      -p)
        for path in "$@"; do
          mode=$(stat -c '%A' -- "$path")
          mode=${mode:1}
          user=${mode:0:3}; user=${user//-/}
          group=${mode:3:3}; group=${group//-/}
          other=${mode:6:3}; other=${other//-/}
          printf 'u=%s,g=%s,o=%s\n' "$user" "$group" "$other"
        done ;;
      -P)
        mask=$1; shift
        for path in "$@"; do
          mode=$(stat -c '%a' -- "$path")
          printf '%o\n' "$((8#$mode & 8#$mask))"
        done ;;
    esac
  }
fi
umask 027
: > group-readable
mkdir public-directory
umask 077
: > private
umask 022
finfo -o group-readable public-directory private
finfo -p group-readable private
finfo -P 0640 group-readable private

cases.purpose: Set the sticky bit on a private regular fixture and compare finfo -o/-P with GNU stat. GNU reports mode 1777; the pinned implementation omits the sticky bit from both octal outputs, so this assertion preserves the confirmed incompatibility.
Compare numeric and named UID/GID fields against GNU stat for the same private fixture owner.

Compare link counts to GNU stat and check portable identity invariants: two hardlink names share an inode/file ID, a distinct live file differs, and files share a device. Raw inode numbers are intentionally not compared across separate fixture roots.
cases.script:
if ! builtin type finfo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  finfo() {
    local option=$1 format
    shift
    case $option in
      -n) format='%h' ;;
      -i) format='%i' ;;
      -d) format='%d' ;;
      -f) format='%d:%i' ;;
    esac
    stat -c "$format" -- "$@"
  }
fi
printf 'linked data' > original
ln original hardlink
: > distinct
finfo -n original hardlink distinct
inode1=$(finfo -i original)
inode2=$(finfo -i hardlink)
inode3=$(finfo -i distinct)
[[ $inode1 =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $inode1 == "$inode2" && $inode1 != "$inode3" ]]
device1=$(finfo -d original)
device2=$(finfo -d distinct)
[[ $device1 =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $device1 == "$device2" ]]
fileid1=$(finfo -f original)
fileid2=$(finfo -f hardlink)
fileid3=$(finfo -f distinct)
[[ $fileid1 =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ && $fileid1 == "$fileid2" && $fileid1 != "$fileid3" ]]
printf 'inode, device, and file-ID relationships agree\n'

cases.purpose: Compare -l target strings and -s symlink sizes with GNU readlink/stat for a target containing spaces and a dangling symlink; tree comparison also checks symlink targets.
cases.script:
if ! builtin type finfo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  finfo() {
    local option=$1
    shift
    if [[ ${1-} == -- ]]; then shift; fi
    case $option in
      -l) readlink -- "$@" ;;
      -s) stat -c '%s' -- "$@" ;;
    esac
  }
fi
printf 'target bytes' > 'target file'
ln -s 'target file' 'link with spaces'
ln -s 'missing target' dangling
finfo -l -- 'link with spaces' dangling
finfo -s -- 'link with spaces' dangling

cases.purpose: Compare numeric atime/mtime/ctime to GNU stat and independently encode ctime-style dates with Bash printf under the runner's C locale and UTC. Assertions use a creation-time window so timestamps remain comparable across fresh reference/candidate roots.
cases.script:
if ! builtin type finfo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  finfo() {
    local option=$1 format path value rendered
    shift
    case $option in
      -a|-A) format='%X' ;;
      -m|-M) format='%Y' ;;
      -c|-C) format='%Z' ;;
    esac
    for path in "$@"; do
      value=$(stat -c "$format" -- "$path")
      case $option in
        -A|-M|-C)
          printf -v rendered '%(%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y)T' "$value"
          printf '%s\n' "$rendered" ;;
        *) printf '%s\n' "$value" ;;
      esac
    done
  }
fi
printf -v start '%(%s)T' -1
printf 'time data' > timestamp
atime=$(finfo -a timestamp)
mtime=$(finfo -m timestamp)
ctime=$(finfo -c timestamp)
printf -v end '%(%s)T' -1
[[ $mtime =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $atime == "$mtime" && $ctime == "$mtime" && $mtime -ge $start && $mtime -le $end ]]
printf -v expected '%(%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y)T' "$mtime"
[[ $(finfo -A timestamp) == "$expected" ]]
[[ $(finfo -M timestamp) == "$expected" ]]
[[ $(finfo -C timestamp) == "$expected" ]]
printf 'numeric timestamps and ctime-style formatting agree\n'

cases.purpose: Compare the documented nonzero failure for a missing file using GNU stat as the independent oracle; diagnostic wording is allowed to differ while its presence and the command status are checked.
cases.script:
if ! builtin type finfo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  finfo() { shift; stat -c '%s' -- "$@"; }
fi
if finfo -s missing; then
  rc=0
else
  rc=$?
fi
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check the documented -P octal mask contract rejects an invalid mask with a nonzero status and diagnostic; this option-parse failure has no GNU stat equivalent.
Check Bash registers finfo as a builtin and exposes its documented help summary.
cases.stdout: builtin registration and help text are available
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t finfo)
doc=$(help finfo)
[[ $kind == builtin && $doc == *'Display information about file attributes.'* ]]
printf 'builtin registration and help text are available\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise the full-summary major/minor and device-type fields for character and block nodes.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed privileged fixture builder that can create synthetic character and block device nodes with known major/minor values and remove them afterward. The provided unprivileged fixture sandbox cannot safely create such nodes; no device operation is executed here.
